Definition: a fountain, bowl or globe (all as round)
BiblicalUsage: In the Old Testament, gullâh is the word for a fountain, bowl or globe (all as round). In 1 Kings 7:41, the text says "and the [two] bowls of the chapiters that [were] on the top of the two pillars." The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gullâh shows us that worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
